## 1. The Conceptual Shift: The Moving Frame (Repère Mobile)

Planar curves are governed by the moving Frenet-Serret orthonormal frame $(\mathbf{T}, \mathbf{N})$:
$$\begin{pmatrix} \mathbf{T}' \\ \mathbf{N}' \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & \kappa \\ -\kappa & 0 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} \mathbf{T} \\ \mathbf{N} \end{pmatrix}$$
By the Fundamental Theorem of Planar Curves, any regular curve is uniquely determined up to rigid Euclidean motion by its curvature invariant $\kappa(s)$.

---

## 2. Numerical Computation: Curve Reconstruction from Curvature

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## Python 3
```python
import numpy as np

def reconstruct_curve_2d(kappa_fn, s_max: float = 3.0, n: int = 1000):
    s = np.linspace(0.0, s_max, n)
    ds = s[1] - s[0]
    theta = np.cumsum([kappa_fn(si) for si in s]) * ds
    x = np.cumsum(np.cos(theta)) * ds
    y = np.cumsum(np.sin(theta)) * ds
    return x[-1], y[-1]

# Euler spiral / clothoid: kappa(s) = 2*s
xf, yf = reconstruct_curve_2d(lambda s: 2.0 * s, 3.0)
print(f"Python 3: Clothoid End at s=3.0: x = {xf:.4f}, y = {yf:.4f}")
```

## C++20
```cpp
#include <iostream>
#include <cmath>
#include <iomanip>

int main() {
    int n = 1000;
    double s_max = 3.0, ds = s_max / n;
    double theta = 0.0, x = 0.0, y = 0.0;

    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        double s = i * ds;
        double kappa = 2.0 * s;
        theta += kappa * ds;
        x += std::cos(theta) * ds;
        y += std::sin(theta) * ds;
    }
    std::cout << std::fixed << std::setprecision(4);
    std::cout << "C++20:    Clothoid End at s=3.0: x = " << x << ", y = " << y << "\n";
    return 0;
}
```

## Julia
```julia
n = 1000; ds = 3.0 / n
s = (0:n-1) .* ds
kappa = 2.0 .* s
theta = cumsum(kappa) .* ds
x = sum(cos.(theta) .* ds)
y = sum(sin.(theta) .* ds)
println("Julia:    Clothoid End at s=3.0: x = $(round(x, digits=4)), y = $(round(y, digits=4))")
```

## Modern Fortran
```fortran
program clothoid
  implicit none
  integer, parameter :: n = 1000
  integer :: i
  real(8) :: ds, s, kappa, theta, x, y

  ds = 3.0d0 / n
  theta = 0.0d0; x = 0.0d0; y = 0.0d0

  do i = 0, n-1
    s = i * ds
    kappa = 2.0d0 * s
    theta = theta + kappa * ds
    x = x + cos(theta) * ds
    y = y + sin(theta) * ds
  end do

  print '(A,F8.4,A,F8.4)', "Fortran:  Clothoid End at s=3.0: x = ", x, ", y = ", y
end program clothoid
```

## Lean 4
```lean
-- Lean 4: Planar Moving Frame and Curvature
import Mathlib.Data.Real.Basic

structure PlanarFrame where
  T : ℝ × ℝ
  N : ℝ × ℝ

-- Skew-symmetric Frenet-Serret system in R^2: T' = κ N, N' = -κ T
def PlanarFrenetDeriv (kappa : ℝ) (frame : PlanarFrame) : PlanarFrame :=
  ⟨⟨-kappa * frame.N.1, -kappa * frame.N.2⟩,
   ⟨ kappa * frame.T.1,  kappa * frame.T.2⟩⟩
```
